title: Cavity Re-initialization with Tight Bounds - Recovery from Optimizer Drift
scientific_hypothesis: The score regression from round 3 to round 5 resulted from optimizer drift in the cavity region away from the resonance condition established in rounds 1-2. Re-initializing layers 7-11 to their round-1 baseline thickness values and applying strict ±10 nm box constraints will recover the high-transmittance resonance while allowing fine spectral shaping.
design_principle: Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with frozen outer DBR mirrors and tightly constrained cavity optimization. The cavity layers (7-11) form the resonant transmission peak, while outer layers (1-6 and 12-21) provide stopband reflection.
proposed_topology: 21 layers total: Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5 on Fused Silica substrate
manufacturing_considerations: ±10 nm tolerance on cavity layers enables practical deposition monitoring
Outer mirrors frozen to reduce fabrication complexity
theory_basis: Defective DBR bandpass filter theory: cavity layers create transmission resonance within DBR stopband
Quarter-wave optical thickness principle for DBR mirrors
expected_advantages: Prevents optimizer from wandering away from verified resonance condition
Maintains high peak transmittance while allowing spectral fine-tuning
Reduces search space to focus on cavity refinement only
known_risks: Tight bounds may prevent discovery of better cavity configurations
Round-1 baseline may not be optimal starting point
Frozen outer mirrors may limit overall performance ceiling
execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 Fabry-Perot bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: Ta2O5(1)/SiO2(2)/Ta2O5(3)/SiO2(4)/Ta2O5(5)/SiO2(6)/Ta2O5(7)/SiO2(8)/Ta2O5(9)/SiO2(10)/Ta2O5(11)/SiO2(12)/Ta2O5(13)/SiO2(14)/Ta2O5(15)/SiO2(16)/Ta2O5(17)/SiO2(18)/Ta2O5(19)/SiO2(20)/Ta2O5(21). Initialize layers 1-6 and 12-21 to frozen values from iteration_10 best candidate. Initialize layers 7-11 to baseline values [187.13, 192.43, 217.30, 235.01, 223.53] nm with optimization bounds ±10 nm from these values. Evaluate coherent TMM transmittance at 1550 nm (target maximize) and 1400-1500 nm, 1600-1700 nm bands (target minimize). Normal incidence, unpolarized light. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Score regression from 0.9757 to 0.7682 indicates optimizer drift in cavity region. Re-initializing to round-1 baseline with tight bounds tests whether the previous high-performing resonance condition can be recovered and stabilized.
